metadata.title: 1980 Case 49
metadata.original_presentation: A 50-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital because of fever and abdominal pain.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: Diabetes mellitus diagnosed 15 years ago, regulated with diet and isophane insulin. Primary hypothyroidism diagnosed 2 years ago, treated with levothyroxine.

teaching_points.content: Diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism are common comorbidities that can complicate the clinical picture.

required.content: What previous surgical history does the patient have?
required.response: Cholecystectomy performed 13 months before admission due to salmonella infection of the gallbladder.

teaching_points.content: Cholecystectomy is a common procedure for gallbladder infections and stones.

required.content: What symptoms did the patient experience before admission?
required.response: Nausea, vomiting, increased drainage from incision, epigastric pain, fever, dark urine.

teaching_points.content: Symptoms like nausea, vomiting, and fever can indicate an infectious process or complication post-surgery.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Biliary Tract Infection
supporting_evidence: history of cholecystectomy due to salmonella infection
refuting_evidence: no specific mention of jaundice or right upper quadrant pain

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pancreatitis
refuting_evidence: no mention of elevated lipase or amylase
no history of alcohol use or gallstones

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Surgical Site Infection
refuting_evidence: no specific mention of erythema or tenderness at the incision site
additional_information_needed: physical examination of the incision site

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Urinary Tract Infection
refuting_evidence: abdominal pain is epigastric rather than suprapubic
no mention of dysuria or frequency

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
refuting_evidence: no mention of hyperglycemia or ketonuria
patient's diabetes is regulated

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: Jaundice, appeared acutely ill, few rales at lung bases, normal heart, scaphoid abdomen with normal bowel sounds, tenderness and fullness at right upper quadrant scar, purulent fluid from sinus.

teaching_points.content: Jaundice and purulent drainage can indicate liver dysfunction and infection.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Biliary Tract Infection (e.g., Cholangitis)
supporting_evidence: tenderness and fullness at right upper quadrant
refuting_evidence: normal bowel sounds

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Abdominal Abscess
supporting_evidence: tenderness and fullness at right upper quadrant scar
refuting_evidence: normal bowel sounds

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pancreatitis
refuting_evidence: normal bowel sounds
no mention of elevated lipase/amylase

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Hepatitis
refuting_evidence: tenderness and fullness at right upper quadrant scar
purulent fluid from sinus

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
refuting_evidence: no mention of hyperglycemia or ketonuria
normal bowel sounds

required.content: What were the laboratory test results?
required.response: Urine positive for protein, glucose, bile; hematocrit 38.6%, WBC 9800; glucose 245 mg/dL; conjugated bilirubin 4 mg/dL; SGOT 865 U/mL; alkaline phosphatase 348 IU/L.

teaching_points.content: Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin suggest liver dysfunction or biliary obstruction.

required.response: Ultrasound showed irregular sonolucent structure beneath skin, consistent with fluid collection or abscess; normal common hepatic duct.

teaching_points.content: Ultrasound is useful for identifying fluid collections and abscesses.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Abdominal abscess
refuting_evidence: none noted
additional_information_needed: CT scan of the abdomen for further evaluation

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Biliary obstruction
refuting_evidence: normal common hepatic duct on ultrasound
additional_information_needed: MRCP or ERCP to evaluate bile ducts

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Hepatitis
refuting_evidence: no specific viral hepatitis markers provided

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
refuting_evidence: absence of ketones in urine
no mention of acidosis

teaching_points.content: Antibiotics are crucial in managing bacterial infections, especially in post-surgical patients.

final_diagnosis.name: Subhepatic abscess with Salmonella infection
supporting_evidence: Positive culture for Salmonella from sinus tract
